newsitem.title: TOGO: Burundi hopes April talks will end blockade.
newsitem.headline: Burundi hopes April talks will end blockade.

text.p: President Paul Buyoya said on Thursday Burundi had begun a national debate on a return to democracy and that it was time for its neighbours to lift sanctions.
Buyoya told a news conference in Togo on the sidelines of an Organisation of African Unity summit on Zaire that the blockade was killing the peace process.
"We hope that this blockade will soon be lifted... We expect the blockade to be completely lifted," he said. "It is killing the peace process."
A declaration from the OAU leaders welcomed the holding in Arusha on April 8 of a meeting to discuss the sanctions.
But one Burundian delegate said a prior meeting of political parties could be used as an excuse to leave some of the sanctions in place if it showed that deep divisions remained.
"We are going to rebuild democracy," said Buyoya, who took office after the Tutsi-dominated army seized power last year. "The process has begun. We have fixed a notional transition of three years."
He said that the government had two priorities -- order and security and then political dialogue.
"There must be order and security," he said, adding that this was essential to open the way to dialogue.
